subject: Post-call: ZenPay inference cost playbook & pilot plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@zenpay.io>
Cc: Andrew Cole <andrew@zenpay.io>
Date: 2026-05-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — inference pain points, goals, and next steps

Hi Priya / Andrew,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid run-through of ZenPay’s payments assistant workload. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on pain, goals, and proposed next steps.

Pain points you emphasized
- Cost: current hosted spend for inference has spiked ~30% month-over-month and the exec team wants better unit economics before expanding to more product flows.
- Latency variability: intermittent 95/99p spikes during peak batch settlement windows causing UX timeouts.
- Predictability: procurement needs a predictable runway and a clear estimate for a pilot so you can justify a committed spend.

Goals you want to hit
- Reduce per-inference unit cost by at least 40% versus current hosted baseline.
- Achieve stable p99 latency under ~200ms for the conversational checkout flow.
- Run a 2–4 week pilot with observable metrics and an ROI snapshot to present to the finance team.

Key levers we discussed to hit those goals
- Batching: moving from single-request serving to micro-batches (avg batch size 6–12) for the denser parts of your pipeline — expected 25–45% token-cost reduction depending on request size.
- KV prefix / prefix-caching: for repeated prompts (merchant prompts, templates) we typically see 15–30% token savings and reduced compute.
- Quantization + model variant routing: use an int8 quantized variant during non-critical responses to shave GPU time/cost; fall back to full-precision for high-safety responses.
- Dedicated capacity option: a small reserved pool gives predictable unit costs and better p99 control vs pure hosted bursting.

Rough economics (ballpark, for sizing conversation)
- Current hosted baseline: ~1.1M tokens/day across the assistant flows (avg request 450 tokens).
- Estimated cost today (hosted mix): ~$2,200/day.
- With batching + caching + quantized inference we estimate a 40–55% reduction in token-equivalent spend (~$990–$1,320/day).
- Dedicated small pool (reserved throughput for peak windows) historically yields ~60–70% lower per-token GPU cost for sustained load, but requires a short commit or pilot agreement.

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll send a short pilot playbook with a pricing estimate and recommended config (attached).
2) If you’re okay, we propose a 2‑week pilot: 100k discounted token credit + dedicated small pool during settlement hours for p99 profiling.
3) Marissa (cc’d) will help setup ingestion & eval prompts and define the success criteria.
4) If the pilot shows the expected win, we’ll put together a 3‑month reserved plan and an ROI summary for finance.

Action items from you
- Confirm interest in the 2‑week pilot and any procurement constraints.
- Share an initial sample of the conversational workload (anonymized) so we can run a small offline estimate.

I’ll follow up shortly with the playbook and a one‑page pricing estimate. Appreciate the time today — happy to hop on another quick call if you want to walk this through with finance.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@zenpay.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Cole <andrew@zenpay.io>
Date: 2026-05-22T17:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — inference pain points, goals, and next steps

Thanks Sergio — this aligns well with what we discussed. A couple of clarifying points before we commit to the pilot:

- Can you confirm the assumptions behind the current ~1.1M tokens/day estimate? Our billing team reports ~900k tokens/day on average but there are spikes on settlement days.
- For the dedicated pool, what minimum commit (hours/day or $/month) should we expect for the smallest profile that still gives the 60% cost benefit?
- We’ll need a short SOW for procurement that lists deliverables, timeline, and data handling assurances (SOC2 controls).

Andrew and I will pull an anonymized sample of the busiest two days and share by EOD Friday. If you can include the pilot SOW + a short procurement-friendly pricing table in the playbook that’d be ideal.

—Priya
Head of Platform, ZenPay
priya@zenpay.io
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@zenpay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — inference pain points, goals, and next steps

Perfect — appreciate the specificity. Quick replies inline and attached the short SOW + pricing table.

- Token baseline: we used the conservative figure of 1.1M tokens/day to allow headroom for the settlement spikes you mentioned (your billing median of ~900k fits inside that). When you send the two busiest days we’ll run a spike-aware sizing.

- Minimum commit for dedicated pool: for the small reserved profile we recommend a 4‑week pilot commitment covering peak window reservations (~8 hours/day) — typical cost exposure for ZenPay’s size would be in the $5k–$8k range for the pilot commitment. This gives you the 50–65% per-token cost advantage during reserved hours.

- SOW and procurement table: attached. Highlights:
  * Scope: 2‑week technical pilot + 2 weeks of observation (total 4 weeks), config for prefix caching, micro-batching, and int8 quantized variant tests.
  * Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 latency report, token spend delta, sample prompt regressions, and an ROI sheet.
  * Data controls: we’ll use customer-keyed encryption for pilot logs and provide SOC2 artifacts; Marissa will coordinate the evidence bundle with your security team.

Estimated pilot outcomes (conservative / optimistic):
- Conservative: 35% cost reduction (mainly batching + caching), p99 improvement to ~230ms.
- Optimistic: 55% cost reduction (batching + 30% cache hitrate + quantized routing), p99 improvement to ~160ms.

Next steps
1) You share the anonymized busiest-day samples (Andrew / Priya).
2) I’ll have Marissa send the SOW + procurement table and loop Ben (solutions engineer) to scope integration effort and required credentials.
3) We’ll schedule a kickoff for next week to onboard and enable metrics.

If this looks good I’ll mark the HubSpot deal HP-12345 as pilot-proposed and send a DocuSign SOW link.

Thanks —
Sergio
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
